verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              उत्थितायां पृथायां तु सुभद्रा भ्रातरं तदा। दृष्ट्वा चुक्रोश दुःखार्ता वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said After Kunti had sat up, Subhadra, seeing her brother, began to weep aloud, and stricken with excessive grief, said, O you having eyes like lotus-petals, look at the grandson of Arjuna of great intelligence! Alas, the Kururace having been thinned, a child has been born that is feeble and dead.

verses.sanskrit: पुण्डरीकाक्ष पश्य त्वं पौत्रं पार्थस्य धीमतः। परिक्षीणेषु कुरुषु परिक्षीणं गतायुषम्॥२॥
इषीका द्रोणपुत्रेण भीमसेनार्थमुद्यता। सोत्तरायां निपतिता विजये मयि चैव ह॥३॥
verses.english: The blade of grass, uplifted by Drona's son for bringing about the destruction of Bhimasena, fell upon Uttara and Vijaya and myself.

verses.sanskrit: सेयं विदीर्णे हृदये मयि तिष्ठति केशव। यन्न पश्यामि दुर्धर्ष सहपुत्रं तु तं प्रभो॥४॥
verses.english: Alas, that blade, O Keshava, is still existing (unexpected) in me, after having pierced my heart, since I do not, O irresistible hero, see this child with iny son.

verses.sanskrit: किं नु वक्ष्यति धर्मात्मा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनार्जुनौ चापि माद्रवत्याः सुतौ च तौ॥५॥
verses.english: What will the righteous-souled king Yudhishthira the just say? What will Bhimasena and Arjuna, and the two sons of Madravati also say?

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वाभिमन्योस्तनयं जातं च मृतमेव च। मुषिता इव वार्ष्णेय द्रोणपुत्रेण पाण्डवाः॥६॥
verses.english: Hearing that Abhimanyu's son was born and dead, the Pandavas, O you of Vrishni's race, will consider themselves as imposed upon by Ashvatthaman.

verses.sanskrit: अभिमन्युः प्रियः कृष्ण भ्रातॄणां नात्र संशयः। ते श्रुत्वा किं नु वक्ष्यन्ति द्रोणपुत्रास्त्रनिर्जिताः॥७॥
भवितातः परं दुःखं किं तदन्यज्जनार्दन। अभिमन्योः सुतात्कृष्ण मृताज्जातादरिन्दम॥८॥
verses.english: Bowing grief, O Janardana, can be greater than this, viz., that Abhimanyu's son should be born and dead?

verses.sanskrit: साहं प्रसादये कृष्ण त्वामद्य शिरसा नता। पृथेयं द्रौपदी चैव ताः पश्य पुरुषोत्तम॥९॥
verses.english: Bowing to you with my head, O Krishna, I seek to please you today! See O foremost of men, these two standing here, viz., Pritha and Draupadi.

verses.sanskrit: यदा द्रोणसुतो गर्भान्पाण्डूनां हन्ति माधव। तदा किल त्वया द्रौणिः क्रुद्धनोक्तोऽरिमर्दन॥१०॥
verses.english: When, O Madhava, the son of Drona tried to destroy the embryos even in the wombs of the ladies of the Pandavas, at that time, O grinder of enemies, you said in anger to Dronas son (even these words). O wretch of a Brahmana, O vilest of men I shall disappoint your wish! I shall revive the son of Kiritin's son.

verses.sanskrit: अकामं त्वां करिष्यामि ब्रह्मबन्धो नराधम। अहं सञ्जीवयिष्यामि किरीटितनयात्मजम्॥११॥
इत्येतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा जानानाहं बलं तव। प्रसादये त्वां दुर्धर्ष जीवतामभिमन्युजः॥१२॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of yours and wellknowing your power, I seek to gratify you, O irresistible hero! Let the son of Abhimanyu be revived.

verses.sanskrit: यद्येतत्त्वं प्रतिश्रुत्य न करोषि वचः शुभम्। सकलं वृष्णिशार्दूल मृतां मामवधारय॥१३॥
verses.english: If having pledged yourself previously you do not accomplish your auspicious vow, do you then know for certain, O chief of the Vrishni race, that I shall put an end to my life.

verses.sanskrit: अभिमन्योः सुतो वीर न सञ्जीवति यद्ययम्। जीवति त्वयि दुर्धर्ष किं करिष्याम्यहं त्वया॥१४॥
verses.english: If, O hero, this son of Abhimanyu does not revive when you, O irresistible one, are alive and near, of what other use will you be to me?

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जीवयैनं दुर्धर्ष मृतं त्वमभिमन्युजम्। सदृशाक्षसुतं वीर सस्यं वर्षन्निवाम्बुदः॥१५॥
verses.english: Do you, therefore, O irresistible one, revive this son of Abhimanyu, this child who has eyes similar to his, even as a rain-charged cloud revives the lifeless crops (on a field).

verses.sanskrit: त्वं हि केशव धर्मात्मा सत्यवान्सत्यविक्रमः। स तां वाचमृतां कर्तुमर्हसि त्वमरिन्दम॥१६॥
verses.english: You, O Keshava, are righteous-souled, truthful, and of prowess incapable of being baffled. You should, O chastiser of enemies make your words truthful.

verses.sanskrit: इच्छन्नपि हि लोकांस्त्रीन्जीवयेथा मृतानिमान्। किं पुनर्दयितं जातं स्वस्रीयस्यात्मजं मृतम्॥१७॥
verses.english: If only you wish it, you can revive the three worlds (of being) if dead! What need, I say, therefore, of this darling child, born but dead, of your sister's son?

verses.sanskrit: प्रभावज्ञास्मि ते कृष्ण तस्मात्त्वां याचयाम्यहम्। कुरुष्व पाण्डुपुत्राणामिमं परमनुग्रहम्॥१८॥
verses.english: I know your power, O Krishna! Therefore do I solicit you! Do you show this great favour to the sons of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: स्वसेति वा महाबाहो हतपुत्रेति वा पुनः। प्रपन्ना मामियं चेति दयां कर्तुमिहार्हसि॥१९॥
verses.english: You should, O mighty-armed one, show mercy to this Uttara, or to me, thinking that I am your sister or even a mother who has lost her son, and one who has thrown herself upon your protection.
